anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs satisfy the fact: each is a separate `gauntlet: question` turn that asks for the operator's reading, invents no reading, claims no retry or write, and shows neither ticket's retry/skip gate or a numeric menu. After is the cleaner of the two — the `#### acme/widget#12` heading and a bare 'type the reading' prompt — but two edges are worth tightening. First, the trailing 'or skip' re-surfaces half of the recovery gate the operator just answered; since the human already chose retry, drop it (or defer skip to a later gate) so the question turn asks for exactly one thing. Second, Before's closing line ('No retry has been dispatched and nothing has been written… #15's report is still waiting') makes the no-retry/no-write/no-sibling state explicit; After relies on silence. A one-line footer such as 'No retry dispatched yet; acme/widget#15 waits for its own turn' would keep that assurance without reintroducing the gate, a menu, or any guessed reading. Also note that Before's A/B/C lettered options skirt the 'numeric menu' prohibition only by not being numeric — After's free-text prompt is the safer pattern to keep.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After satisfies the fact cleanly: it opens a question turn, asks the operator to type the AC reading, and makes no claims about a retry, a write, or either ticket's gate. Before fails because it pre-composes candidate readings (A/B/C) and presents them as a menu—the assistant authored the readings instead of waiting for the operator's, which a careful reader counts as inventing a reading and offering a menu, even though the labels are letters rather than numbers; it also drags ticket 15 back into the turn. To keep the fact while delivering the Change, keep After's shape (one question, no options list, no sibling mention); if you want the retry context visible, prefix only a single line naming acme/widget#12 under its own heading and still ask for a typed reading rather than listing choices.
